To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we report a novel ternary composite electrode based on macroporous Ni/C, MnO2 and OMC, for solid state super-capacitors with high performance, and the device is flexible and can be twisted without capacity fading.

a novel ternary electrode based on MnO2 spheres coated on a macro/mesoprous Ni foam and OMC was developed, and a flexible supercapacitor device with high volumetric energy density and power density was fabricated.

the utilization efficiency of active material in MnO2 based all solid state super capacitor is enhanced by using a ternary system electrode composed of MnO2 spheres, Ni foam and mesoporous carbon membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design, fabrication, and characterization of a novel ternary system composed by hierarchical MnO2 sphere as the active materials, macroporous nickel foam as gel penetratable skeletons, and OMC as the charge- transfer accelerating layer.
the fabrication of a novel ternary system based on hierarchical MnO2 sphere/Ni foam/OMC membrane for solid state super capacitors.
a high performance flexible solid state all solid state super capacitor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ternary electrode based solid state super-capacitors have been successfully developed for the first time.
the present work provides a novel electrode for flexible solid state supercapcitors with high energy density, excellent cycling stability and high flexibility.
the ternary MnO2/Ni foam/OMC electrode with the ionic conducting BMIMCl gel as the solid electrolyte is a promising candidate for flexible supercapacitors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hierarchical MnO2 sphere/Ni/OMC electrode is a promising candidate to replace the traditional metal foil current collector in flexible solid state supercapcitors.
a ternary system of macroporous Ni foams, mesoporous carbon membrane and MnO2 spheres is proposed for the first time as the electrode for solid state MnO2 supercapacitors.
a flexible all solid state high-performance supercapacitor has been developed by employing a ternary system as the electrode and BMIMCl-modified gel electrolyte.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a ternary system of macroporous Ni, OMC, and MnO2 is an ideal structure for solid state super-capacitors.
a hierarchical macro/mesopores architecture is a highly efficient strategy for improving energy storage devices.
the combination of macro/mesoscale materials with gel electrolytes provides a promising route to design high performance solid state supercapcitors with high volumetric energy density.
